_comment: RUNTIME LADDER for the privileged-baseline claim. The campaign measured the spectral oracles at runtimes 1, 4 and 12 and found the gap to equal-budget search at +0.054, +0.167 and +0.111 -- decisive at every point and not closing. That is three points over one decade, and the gap is non-monotonic, so it licenses no extrapolation in either direction. This extends the axis to 12, 36 and 108 to test directly whether the local-adiabatic rule catches up given more time, which is the single strongest objection to the finding. Physical size is capped at 10 because a full spectral teacher is, so this varies runtime and nothing else. Logical size is fixed at 4 and only the runtime varies: parents are split per (family, logical_size) cell, so three sizes over four families would need 12 cells and leave too few parents in each. Holding size fixed keeps the cells at four and the comparison one-dimensional, which is what a ladder is for.
